title: ReactNative: Migrate ondevice addons from `addons`
description:
Closes https://github.com/storybookjs/react-native/issues/873

## What I did

On-device addons listed in `addons` cause `extract` (story indexing / manifest generation) to fail in `@storybook/react-native` projects because Storybook Core attempts to evaluate them as presets in a Node.js context. The on-device addons contain React Native code that cannot be loaded server-side, resulting in a `CriticalPresetLoadError`.

The fix moves on-device addons to a separate `deviceAddons` field that is only consumed at runtime (by `scripts/generate.js`), not by Core.

### Changes

- **New automigration** (`rn-ondevice-addons-to-device-addons`) — detects `@storybook/react-native` projects and moves any addon whose name contains `"ondevice"` from `addons` → `deviceAddons`; preserves both string and object (`{ name, options }`) forms
- **Registered** in `allFixes` immediately after `rnstorybookConfig`
- **9 tests** covering: guard conditions (no RN, no ondevice addons), string/object addon detection, deps vs devDeps, and run-phase behavior (removal, object preservation, dryRun passthrough)
- **MIGRATION.md** — added `React Native: on-device addons moved to deviceAddons` section (with TOC entry and before/after example) in the 9.x → 10.0.0 chapter

Note: `deviceAddons` is intentionally not added to the shared `StorybookConfigRaw` core type since it is React Native-specific. The automigration uses `ConfigFile`'s string-path APIs to write the field without requiring a type declaration.

**Before / After:**

```ts
// Before (.rnstorybook/main.ts)
export default {
  addons: [
    '@storybook/addon-ondevice-controls',
    '@storybook/addon-ondevice-actions',
    '@storybook/addon-docs',
  ],
};

// After (automigrated)
export default {
  addons: ['@storybook/addon-docs'],
  deviceAddons: [
    '@storybook/addon-ondevice-controls',
    '@storybook/addon-ondevice-actions',
  ],
};
```

<details>
<summary>🧩 Analysis chain</summary>

🌐 Web query:

`In Vitest, if a test imports a module from `./vite-server.ts` but calls `vi.mock('./vite-server', { spy: true })`, is the mock guaranteed to apply to that import, or should the `vi.mock()` specifier exactly match `./vite-server.ts`?`

💡 Result:

Not guaranteed.

Vitest registers mocks against the *module specifier it resolves/handles*, and its transform wraps the *same specifier string* in the generated dynamic import (e.g. `import('./answer.js')` stays `import('./answer.js')` under the hood) [1]. If your SUT imports `./vite-server.ts` but you mock `./vite-server`, the mock will only apply **if** Vitest/Vite resolve `./vite-server` to the same module (which depends on resolver/extension behavior such as `resolve.extensions`) [2]. To be safe/portable, make the specifier match exactly—e.g. `vi.mock(import('./vite-server.ts'), { spy: true })` (or use the exact string your code imports) [1].

**Sources:** [1] [2]
